title: urban-digital-memory
text:
This research explores how citizens’ lived experiences shared on social media (X/Twitter) serve as digital memories that express emotional and spatial values regarding public spaces[cite: 6].
Focusing on City Theater Square in Tehran, the project applies data scraping (via Apify), topic modeling, and sentiment analysis to extract spatial perceptions and link them directly to urban design interventions[cite: 6, 8].
[cite: 7]



Data Scraping & Analysis: Processed tweets from 2022–2026 across spatial topics[cite: 6, 7].
Sentiment-Spatial Association: Mapped positive, negative, and neutral emotions to cognitive elements (paths, nodes, landmarks)[cite: 6, 7].
Design Framework: Created a decision pipeline converting negative-valued spatial associations into targeted urban design responses[cite: 7, 8].

title: Soroush Saffarzadeh
text:
I am an Urbanism Graduate (MSc, TU Delft) specializing at the intersection of Urban Analytics, Spatial Data Science, and Socio-Ecological Urban Design[cite: 1, 3, 4, 10]. My research and practice leverage geospatial analysis, sentiment modeling, and spatial decision-support tools to inform public space design and urban restoration strategies[cite: 1, 6, 9, 10].



Digital Urban Memory & Public Space: Scraping social media data (Twitter/X) to evaluate spatial sentiment and public space interventions[cite: 6].
Spatial Multi-Criteria Decision Analysis (S-MCDA): Quantitative evaluation of urban stream restoration and climate adaptation strategies[cite: 1, 10].
Urban Modeling & Visualization: Integrating R, QGIS, Rhino, CityEngine, and Twinmotion for 3D spatial simulation[cite: 2, 16].








Leveraging social media scraping, sentiment analysis, and topic modeling to inform urban design processes for Tehran’s City Theater Square[cite: 1, 6].



An open-source S-MCDA and K-means clustering analysis project evaluating urban stream restoration principles in Dresden, Germany[cite: 1, 10].
